package.title: What If the Person You Love Forgot Everything Every Few Seconds?
alt_titles: "This Time Properly Awake": The Diary of a Man Who Forgot Every Few Seconds
He Forgot Everything Except His Wife
description: In 1985, the English musician Clive Wearing caught herpes encephalitis. It left him with a memory span of only seconds, which Oliver Sacks called the most devastating case of amnesia ever recorded.
His diary filled with near-identical entries, each crossing out the one before: "2:10 P.M: This time properly awake... 2:14 P.M: this time finally awake... 2:35 P.M: this time completely awake."
He always recognised his wife, Deborah, and greeted her with relief every time. He could still play the piano and conduct.
If you could only keep one thing, what would you keep?
sources: Oliver Sacks (2007), "The Abyss". The New Yorker, 24 September 2007.
Wilson B. A., Baddeley A. D., Kapur N. (1995), Journal of Clinical and Experimental Neuropsychology 17: 668–681.
